title: Data drill: Peak Audio Ltd
intro: Read the case study first. Then choose which calculations are worth doing, work them out, and decide what the numbers show and where you would use them.
caseHtml:
Peak Audio Ltd

Peak Audio Ltd designs headphones in Manchester and has them made by a partner factory. Its oldest product, the Classic over-ear headphones, launched in 2016. Its wireless earbuds, launched in 2023, are growing but face strong competition from Apple, Samsung and Sony.

Peak is about to launch new noise-cancelling earbuds called Peak Air. Its managing director, Imran Ali, is choosing between two launch prices.

questions.text: Analyse one way in which the product life cycle could help Peak Audio Ltd plan its marketing for the Classic headphones.
Assess whether Peak Audio Ltd should stop selling the Classic headphones.
Peak Audio Ltd is choosing between price skimming at £149 and penetration pricing at £89 for Peak Air. Evaluate these two options and recommend which it should choose.

calcs.why: Worth doing. Evidence of where Classic is in its life cycle, and whether to drop it.

meaning.q: What does a fall of 18.75% suggest?
opts: Classic may be entering the decline stage of its life cycle
Classic is in the growth stage
meaning.why: A sharp fall in sales after nine years fits decline, although one year of data is not enough to be sure.

use.why: Evidence of where Classic is in its life cycle, and whether to drop it.

calcs.why: Worth doing. One of the two figures you need to compare the pricing options.

meaning.q: Compared with penetration pricing, what does this show?
opts: Skimming gives less revenue in year one, but a much bigger margin on each pair
Skimming gives more profit for certain
The two give the same revenue
meaning.why: Penetration gives £2,848,000. Skimming earns less in total but more on each unit, so profit depends on costs.

use.why: One of the two figures you need to compare the pricing options.

calcs.why: Worth doing. The other figure for comparing the options.

meaning.q: What else would Imran need to know to choose between the options?
opts: The cost of each pair, to work out which option gives more profit
Nothing, the higher revenue option is always best
meaning.why: Revenue is not profit. With a low price, the margin on each pair might be small.

use.why: The other figure for comparing the options.

calcs.t: Size of the wireless earbuds market
calcs.why: Worth doing. Helps judge whether winning share quickly with a low price is worth it.
calcs.formula: Sales of the business ÷ market share

opts: Peak has a small share of a large market, so there is room to grow if Peak Air can win customers
meaning.why: A £45 million market with a 4% share leaves a lot of potential customers, but bigger brands hold most of it.

use.why: Helps judge whether winning share quickly with a low price is worth it.

calcs.why: There is no information on operating profit or capital employed, and ROCE is not part of these questions.
There are no data on changes in income, so YED cannot be calculated.
